'''Sylvia Vine Sheat Rumball''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|CNZM}} (née '''Sheat'''; born 1939) is a New Zealand scientist and an international expert in scientific research ethics.

== Education ==
Rumball completed a BSc and MSc (1962) at the [[University of Canterbury]]. She moved to the [[University of Auckland]] where she undertook a PhD in chemistry (1966),<ref>{{cite thesis |last=Sheat |first=Sylvia |year=1966 |type=Doctoral thesis |title=Some structural investigations of copper co-ordination compounds. |publisher=ResearchSpace@Auckland, University of Auckland |hdl=2292/56262}}</ref> supervised by Professor (later Sir) [[Neil Waters]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2009-12-18|title=Ethicist and chemist retires after 42 years|url=https://www.massey.ac.nz/massey/about-massey/news/article.cfm?mnarticle_uuid=9EE8396C-96BF-57FE-A318-C7D43B710D37|access-date=2021-08-01|website=Massey University|language=en-NZ}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|date=1939-01-01|title=Rumball, Sylvia Vine, 1939–|url=https://natlib.govt.nz/records/22506329|access-date=2021-08-01|website=National Library of New Zealand|language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==
During her PhD studies, Rumball worked as a junior lecturer at the University of Auckland from 1963 to 1966. She then moved to the [[University of Oxford]] on a postdoctoral fellowship and studied protein crystallography under [[Dorothy Hodgkin]].<ref name=":0" />

Rumball joined [[Massey University]] as a lecturer in 1967.<ref name=":0" /> She was promoted to associate professor in 2000<ref name=":1" /> and to full professor by 2005, when she was also assistant to the Vice Chancellor (Equity and Ethics) at Massey.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2005-05-28|title=Perspectives on bioethics|url=https://www.massey.ac.nz/massey/about-massey/news/article.cfm?mnarticle_uuid=2D9749E3-96BF-57FE-A255-40E6D431ACAB|access-date=2021-08-01|website=Massey University|language=en-NZ}}</ref> She served on the University Council from 2005 to 2008. She was appointed Professor Emeritus in July 2009,<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2009-07-01|title=Commemorative scrolls recognise current and new Professors Emeriti|url=https://www.massey.ac.nz/massey/about-massey/news/article.cfm?mnarticle_uuid=342CD6AB-96BF-57FE-A77E-D2D1DAB41313|access-date=2021-08-01|website=Massey University|language=en-NZ}}</ref> officially retiring in November of the same year.<ref name=":0" />

To celebrate the centenary of women's suffrage in New Zealand, Rumball was selected as one of eight women to give graduation addresses at Massey University in 1993.<ref>{{Citation|author1=|title=Commemorating Women's Achievements: Graduation addresses by women in the centennial year of women's suffrage, 1993|publication-date=1994|editor-last=McIlroy|editor-first=Andrea|publisher=Massey University|isbn=978-0-908665-86-0|author2=|year=1994 }}</ref>

From 2002 to 2011 she was chair of the National Ethics Committee on Assisted Human Reproduction,<ref>{{Cite web|date=2002-07-11|title=Appointments/reappointments to the National Ethics Committee on Assisted Human Reproduction|url=https://gazette.govt.nz/notice/id/2002-go4659|access-date=2021-08-01|website=New Zealand Gazette}}</ref> later known as the Advisory Committee on Assisted Reproductive Technology (ACART).<ref>{{Cite web|date=2008-09-11|title=Appointment/reappointments to the Advisory Committee on Assisted Reproductive Technology (ACART)|url=https://gazette.govt.nz/notice/id/2008-go6528|access-date=2021-08-01|website=New Zealand Gazette}}</ref> She also served on the Drug Free Sport New Zealand Board from 2007 to 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2007-11-08|title=Appointments/reappointment to the Drug Free Sport New Zealand Board|url=https://gazette.govt.nz/notice/id/2007-au7696|access-date=2021-08-01|website=New Zealand Gazette}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2013-02-21|title=Appointment to the Drug Free Sport New Zealand Board|url=https://gazette.govt.nz/notice/id/2013-go901|access-date=2021-08-01|website=New Zealand Gazette}}</ref> Rumball also served on UNESCO's [[International Bioethics Committee]] and the [[International Council for Science]]'s Committee on Freedom and Responsibility in the conduct of Science.<ref name=":0" />

== Honours and awards ==
[[File:Sylvia Rumball receiving CNZM from Sir Anand Satyanand.jpg|thumb|right|Rumball (left) being congratulated by the governor-general, [[Anand Satyanand]], on her investiture as a [[Companion of the New Zealand Order of Merit]] at [[Government House, Wellington]], on 4 April 2008]]
Rumball was appointed an [[Officer of the New Zealand Order of Merit]], for services to science, in the [[1998 Birthday Honours (New Zealand)|1998 Queen's Birthday Honours]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dpmc.govt.nz/publications/queens-birthday-honours-list-1998 |title=Queen's Birthday honours list 1998 |date=1 June 1998 |publisher=Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet |access-date=1 August 2021}}</ref> In the [[2008 New Year Honours (New Zealand)|2008 New Year Honours]], she was promoted to [[Companion of the New Zealand Order of Merit]], also for service to science.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dpmc.govt.nz/publications/new-year-honours-list-2008 |title=New Year honours list 2008 |date=31 December 2007 |publisher=Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet |access-date=1 August 2021}}</ref>
